name: Lugano and Ticino
tagline: Switzerland with an Italian accent, palm-fringed lakes, piazzas, risotto and merlot, three UNESCO castles and a bridge you can jump from.
highlight: Sitting on Lugano's lakefront under a palm tree, with Monte Brè across the water and an espresso in hand.
shortDescription: The Italian-speaking south, with Lugano's lake and piazzas, Locarno and Ascona on Lake Maggiore, the castles of Bellinzona and the Verzasca Valley.
metaDescription: A Lugano and Ticino travel guide: Lake Lugano and Monte Brè, Piazza della Riforma, Locarno and Ascona, Bellinzona castles, Verzasca Valley, merlot, risotto, where to stay and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: Milan Malpensa (MXP) or Lugano (LUG), about 1 hour by train from Milan
knownFor: Lakes, palm trees, Italian food, castles, sunshine
goodFor: Lakeside relaxation, food and wine, castles, sun in spring and autumn

intro: Ticino is the only Swiss canton that is entirely Italian-speaking, and it feels like a different country from the German-speaking north. South of the Alps, palm trees and camellias grow on the shores of Lake Lugano and Lake Maggiore, the air is warmer, and the pace is slower. Espresso replaces filter coffee, risotto and polenta appear on menus, and the wine is merlot.

Lugano is the main city, a lakeside town of about 63,000 people, with an arcaded old town around Piazza della Riforma, a lakefront promenade and funiculars up to Monte Brè and Monte San Salvatore for views over the lake. Ticino's other centres include Locarno and its neighbour Ascona on Lake Maggiore, famous for a film festival and sunshine, and Bellinzona, with three medieval castles that make up a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Beyond the towns are wild valleys of granite, chestnut woods and stone villages. The Verzasca Valley has turquoise water, and the Ponte dei Salti, a stone bridge near Lavertezzo. Ticino is a summer resort, but it is also lovely in spring, when camellias bloom, and autumn, when the chestnuts fall. Three days lets you feel the region, and it is a short train ride through the Gotthard Base Tunnel from Zurich.

whyVisit.intro: Ticino is a sunny, Mediterranean side of Switzerland with excellent food.
